summary_student.text: SAME overheated common spacecraft materials inside a sealed glovebox on the International Space Station to make smoke, and tested how two smoke detectors reacted. Scientists expected smoke particles to grow bigger without gravity, which could stop some detectors from raising an alarm. Knowing this helps build smoke detectors that warn astronauts early.

summary_professional.text: Smoke was generated by overheating spacecraft materials with an igniter run for a predefined period (15 to 60 seconds) in near-field hardware in the Microgravity Science Glovebox with an attached Far Field Box; each combustion event typically lasted 2 minutes. Thermophoretic soot samplers collected particulate later analyzed by Transmission Electron Microscopy for primary and aggregate particle dimensions, sample remains were weighed for mass loss, and video records gave the response of two smoke detectors. Sample temperature, flow field and particle aging time were controlled, and 1-g conditions producing the same mass loss were determined for comparison. Specific sample materials are not stated in PSI.

pillar.reason: SAME provides quantitative data on smoke detector sensitivity to reduced gravity smokes and a baseline for future fire detection technology.

environments.reason: Flown on the International Space Station; results evaluate the existing spacecraft smoke detection technologies.
Aimed at an advanced fire detector for future spacecraft used for long duration missions.
